description: First-ever execution test of TXLEGACY's own internal CLONEDIR-reading logic (tools/qclsrc/txlegacy.clp), which every part05-legacy-probe/part05-gen-probe connection has bypassed so far by compiling the same target objects directly via 'file'/'cl' manifest steps instead of actually CALLing TXLEGACY. TXLEGACY's own CPYFRMSTMF calls (LOADPF/LOADDSPF/LOADRPG/LOADCLP subroutines) all hardcode STMFCCSID(1208), matching what a real learner's real `git clone` produces (per 05-01's own manually-typed CPYFRMSTMF commands, also STMFCCSID(1208)) - but this harness's own heredoc'd 'file' steps produce genuinely CCSID-273-tagged/encoded files (harness-selftest's own finding), which would NOT be a faithful stand-in and would just reproduce that known conversion failure rather than test TXLEGACY itself (advisor review, 2026-09-27). To build a faithful tree: the 9 files are first uploaded as NORMAL 'file' steps into their real QDDSSRC/QRPGSRC/QCLSRC members (the same members part05-legacy-probe already compiles from - this just re-uploads identical source, no conflict), then a set of 'sh' steps runs CPYTOSTMF FROMMBR(...) TOSTMF(...) STMFCCSID(1208) ENDLINFMT(*LF) STMFOPT(*REPLACE) (parameter names confirmed via IBM Docs CPYTOSTMF reference) to convert each member into a genuinely-1208-tagged/encoded IFS stream file at the exact CLONEDIR-relative path TXLEGACY expects (src/legacy/qddssrc|qrpgsrc|qclsrc/*, under $HOME/ibmi-kyozai) - this really does perform an EBCDIC-to-1208 conversion (CPYTOSTMF, unlike setccsid, converts the actual bytes, not just the tag), which should be a faithful stand-in for what a real git-cloned file looks like. TXLEGACY is then compiled and CALLed via QCMDEXC, using a small helper CL program (src/txlegrun.clp, PARM(LIB) only - the 32-byte CALL/PARM literal-padding trap does not apply since LIB's own declared length is 10, well under 32) because (a) the wrapper CL program clgen.mjs builds has no DCL section available to any individual step (see txlegrun.clp's own header), and (b) a literal `TXLEGACY LIB(...)` statement embedded directly in a step's cmd text would fail to compile anyway, since the CL compiler resolves a *CMD's syntax at compile time but TXLEGACY's own *CMD is only created by an earlier step's runtime action inside the same wrapper - the same problem P0-3 already solved for JUCINQ in verify/part06-12-prtf-cpp-swap/manifest.json's PRESWAPRUN/POSTSWAPRUN steps, which this file's approach mirrors. CLONEDIR is omitted from the TXLEGACY call so its own CURUSER-based derivation resolves it to the same $HOME/ibmi-kyozai path the tree was written to. Prerequisite: TXSETUP has already built the sample DB (TOKUIM/JUCHUM/JUCHUD/ZAIKOM/TANTOM) in this library - same prerequisite as every other part05-* manifest, already satisfied from earlier connections in this library. TXLEGACY is called WITHOUT FORCE(*YES) - a DLTDTAARA step removes TXLEGST first (MONMSG CPF0000, harmless if it does not exist) so every run of this manifest is a genuine first-time-load test, not a silent already-loaded no-op on a rerun. CRTCMD is called without REPLACE(*YES) - unlike CRTCLPGM/CRTRPGPGM (confirmed via IBM Docs and this repo's own many working manifests), no primary source in this repo confirms CRTCMD even has a REPLACE parameter, and verify/part06-12-prtf-cpp-swap's own already-reviewed JUCINQ command creation likewise never uses it; a DLTCMD (MONMSG CPF0000) step runs first instead, matching that same established, rerun-safe idiom. Success/failure is NOT judged from DSPOBJD/object existence (TK0100/JU0300/ZA0500/etc. already exist in this library from part05-legacy-probe's own unrelated direct compiles, so their mere presence proves nothing about whether TXLEGACY itself ran) and NOT from the RUNTXLEG step's own MONMSG (TXLEGACY catches its own internal errors and returns normally regardless, per its FAILSAFE label - a missing 'RUNTXLEG FAILED' marker would not mean TXLEGACY succeeded). The real evidence is VFYLOG's own automatic capture of TXLEGACY's SNDPGMMSG output ('TXLEGACY: done...' vs 'TXLEGACY: stopped on an unexpected error' - both messages land in the wrapper's own job log since QCMDEXC->TXLEGACY runs in the same job/call stack), plus txlegrun.clp's own RTVDTAARA+SNDPGMMSG report of TXLEGST's actual value (also captured in VFYLOG) and the collect step below checking each object's real creation timestamp (QSYS2.OBJECT_STATISTICS) to confirm they were recompiled NOW, not just that they exist from before. Risk noted (advisor review, 2026-09-27): docs/part02/02-05-txsetup.md's own real-hardware note records that the 2026-09-25 verification did a real `git clone --sparse` into this same $HOME/ibmi-kyozai path, so this manifest may be writing untracked src/legacy/* files into an actual git working tree - MKTREE now checks for .git first (`ls -d`) so the result records whether that is the case. If so, once Part 5 lands on main, a `git pull` in that directory would abort on the untracked files; cleanup (remove src/legacy there, or re-clone) is noted in work/human-checklist.md for P7.

steps.sql: SELECT OBJNAME, OBJTYPE, OBJCREATED FROM TABLE(QSYS2.OBJECT_STATISTICS('&LIB', '*ALL')) X WHERE OBJNAME IN ('TXLEGST', 'TK0100', 'JU0300', 'ZA0500', 'JU0900C', 'MN0000C') ORDER BY OBJNAME
